title: Expose the exact shell-energy flux and spatial tail-mobility quantity
statement: In the stipulated spatially local Coulomb LFD normalization, g=f(1-f), ell=log(f/(1-f)) and a(z)=Pi(z)/|z| give d_t integral phi f=-1/2 integral_xvw gg (grad phi(v)-grad phi(w))^T a(v-w)(grad ell(v)-grad ell(w)). Its absolute value is at most sqrt(D(f) A_phi). For phi_R=|v-u|^2 chi(|v-u|/R), the quadratic energy gradient cancels under Pi(v-w), and A_phi_R<=C_chi integral_x rho^(2/3)e_R, where e_R=integral_|v-u|>R |v-u|^2 f dv. Finite-horizon mobility vanishes as R grows; the cumulative outward cutoff flux tends to Delta as t tends to infinity then R grows. The accepted unit-window rho^2 estimate controls this only through the still-unbounded unit-window integral e_R^(3/2). No uniform infinite-time tail-mobility estimate or Delta=0 follows.
